in_text_mentions: At presentation, the significant findings on clinical examination were extensive verrucae on both hands and feet, and chronic lymphoedema of the left leg (Figure 2). There were no skeletal abnormalities. His chest x‐ray was normal and in particular, showed no features of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis. He had severe pancytopenia with a low reticulocyte production index (RPI). There were no records of blood counts prior to this presentation. Blood counts, lymphocyte subsets and immunoglobulin fractions are shown in Table 1. Vaccine responses were normal.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Axial chest CT at age 26 in a patient with GATA2 deficiency shows subpleural reticulation and interlobular septal thickening, consistent with the article-reported progressive interstitial lung disease / PAP-spectrum pulmonary manifestation. b: Axial chest CT at age 36 shows progression with ground-glass and nodular opacities in a patient with GATA2 deficiency and early-onset progressive ILD; the ground-glass plus septal thickening supports the pulmonary alveolar proteinosis finding key. c: Axial chest CT at age 41 shows worsening interlobular septal thickening with ground-glass and nodular opacities in GATA2 deficiency with progressive ILD; the combination supports the pulmonary alveolar proteinosis CT finding.

plate_findings.evidence: A BME showed a hypocellular bone marrow with trilineage dysplasia

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Bone marrow trephine histology from a patient with GATA2 deficiency (article title: case report of GATA2 deficiency) showing a small non-caseating granuloma with hypocellular marrow background, matching the caption 'multiple small granulomas' and in-text description of hypocellular marrow with granulomas and positive mycobacterial culture. B: Second field of the bone marrow biopsy from the GATA2 deficiency patient showing a well-formed granuloma adjacent to bone trabecula and adipose tissue, consistent with the captioned 'multiple small granulomas' in the setting of disseminated mycobacterial infection. C: Third field of the same bone marrow biopsy showing ill-defined small granulomata among hypocellular haematopoietic tissue, supporting the captioned granulomatous marrow involvement in GATA2 deficiency with mycobacterial infection.
panels.attribution_text: Nell et al. Infection and myelodysplasia: A case report of GATA2 deficiency in a South African patient.. Clinical case reports 2023. doi:10.1002/ccr3.7075. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Bone marrow examination showing multiple small granulomas (original magnification 50×).
in_text_mentions: A BME showed a hypocellular bone marrow with trilineage dysplasia and multiple small granulomas (Figure 3). The karyotype was normal and fluorescence in situ hybridisation (FISH) was negative for deletion 5q31/monosomy 5 (MetaSystems Probes GmbH), deletion 7q22q31/monosomy 7 (MetaSystems Probes GmbH), deletion 20q12 (MetaSystems Probes GmbH), trisomy 8 (Vysis IGH/Myc/CEP 8 Tri‐Color, DF FISH Probe, Abbott) and loss of the Y chromosome (Vysis CEP X/Y DNA probe kit, Abbott). Mycobacterial culture of bone marrow aspirate showed acid‐fast bacilli, which was identified by polymerase chain reaction

panels.rationale: H&E section of a cervical lymph node from the reported GATA2-deficient adult showing a granuloma with fibrinoid necrosis; the caption and in-text description attribute this necrotising (lympho)histiocytic/granulomatous proliferation to the patient's GATA2 deficiency-associated lymphadenopathy. Granulomatous lymph node involvement is an unusual (atypical) manifestation rather than a classic GATA2 finding, and the vocabulary lacks a dedicated granuloma term, so the lymphadenopathy key is used with proposed additional descriptors.
panels.attribution_text: Gabzdilová et al. GATA2 deficiency in an adult with alveolar proteinosis, infections, lymphadenopathy with granulomatosis, and immune deficiency: case report.. Frontiers in immunology 2025. doi:10.3389/fimmu.2025.1608392. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Granuloma with fibrinoid necrosis from cervical lymph node.
in_text_mentions: ia for MDS. Bone marrow morphology and flow cytometry revealed a decrease in monocyte and B lymphocyte counts compared to the normal range. Cervical lymphatic node histology has been described as difficult-to-classify necrotising (lympho) histiocytic (granulomatous) proliferation, suggesting a primary consideration of systemic immunopathological disease, with infectious disease being less likely. No convincing signs of malignancy were observed (Figure 2). Shortly after the initial evaluation, the patient experienced an episode of immune thrombocytopenia with prompt response to corticosteroids.
